task.title: Compose explicitly selected skills into tool-free turns
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/657 by giving callers a provider-neutral tool-free request boundary with explicit skill selection and structurally distinct authority fields.
acceptance_criteria: Reject duplicate or missing exact skill IDs deterministically before persistence or provider invocation.
Expose system policy, developer policy, exact-ID-ordered selected skills, and durable transcript as distinct typed provider fields in descending authority order.
Exclude registered but unselected skills and keep existing runtime APIs skill-free unless the composed API is explicitly called.
Preserve human-turn-first durable ordering and source-preserving provider failure behavior.

attempts.summary: Established RED coverage for exact selection and composed turn behavior.
attempts.diagnostic: Focused tests failed because SkillRegistry had no exact-ID selection operation and AssistantRuntime had no composed provider request or execution boundary.
attempts.patch: Added tests for duplicate and missing selection, deterministic ordering, exact text, unselected exclusion, typed request fields, skill-free defaults, and provider failure persistence.

attempts.summary: Implemented deterministic borrowed selection and one provider-neutral composed turn.
attempts.diagnostic: Keeping policy, selected instruction blocks, and transcript as separate typed fields preserved authority classification without kernel prompt concatenation or provider-native role lowering.
attempts.patch: Added SkillSelection, selection errors, ComposedAssistantRequest, ComposedAssistantProvider, execute_composed_turn, documentation, and milestone evidence.

attempts.summary: Confirmed the bounded contract through independent and substantive review.
attempts.diagnostic: Independent review and CodeRabbit found no blocking or actionable issue, so no speculative routing, token budgeting, tool, or serialization behavior was added.
attempts.patch: Kept existing turns behavior-compatible and retained the explicit composed API as the only path by which selected skills influence a provider request.

outcome.summary: Tool-free runtime callers can explicitly select exact registered skills and pass them to providers beneath caller policy and above transcript without changing skill-free defaults.

verification.command: GitHub Rust quality gate https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/actions/runs/30275228556 and substantive exact-head CodeRabbit review at https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/pull/658

lessons: Skill availability becomes request authority only through explicit exact-ID selection by the caller.
Typed provider fields preserve authority ordering more reliably than concatenating a synthetic kernel prompt.
Selection validation belongs before durable transcript mutation and provider invocation.
Registered but unselected instructions must be absent rather than merely assigned lower precedence.
Additive composed APIs preserve conservative skill-free defaults for existing callers.
